display_title: Differential expression profiles of plasma exosomal microRNAs in dilated cardiomyopathy with chronic heart failure
summary: Human plasma exosomal miRNA profiling in DCM with chronic heart failure identified an article-reported 92-feature differential set, computational target networks and external qRT-PCR assessment of 10 hub miRNAs in 10 patients and 6 controls.
research_question: Which plasma exosomal miRNA expression patterns distinguish the studied DCM-with-chronic-heart-failure samples from healthy controls, and which candidate signals were evaluated by an external assay?
author_summary: This human case-control molecular-profiling study used plasma vesicle preparations, small-RNA sequencing, target prediction and external qRT-PCR to investigate DCM with chronic heart failure. The Results report 92 differentially expressed miRNA features, comprising 48 upregulated and 44 downregulated features under the stated screening thresholds. Computational enrichment and network analyses provide biological hypotheses rather than directly measured target regulation. Ten selected hub miRNAs were assessed in an external group of 10 patients and 6 healthy controls, with expression-profile separation reported. The discovery participant count was not reliably established from the reviewed text and is not reconstructed here. miR-185-5p appears in the discovery table and predicted network, but not in the listed 10-miRNA external qRT-PCR panel. The evidence supports exploratory circulating-RNA associations and assay follow-up, not an early-detection test, prospective prognosis or a human causal mechanism.

study_profile.evidence_type: Human molecular association and small external assay evaluation
study_profile.population: Patients with DCM and chronic heart failure compared with healthy individuals; recruitment criteria included LVEF <=45%, NYHA II-IV and heart-failure history longer than 6 months
study_profile.primary_endpoint: Between-group plasma exosomal miRNA expression differences
study_profile.secondary_endpoint: Predicted target/pathway relationships and external hub-miRNA expression-profile evaluation
study_profile.counting_note: Discovery and external assay phases are distinct. The discovery participant count is not reliably established from the reviewed text, so no complete unique-participant total is inferred. Sequencing features, predicted genes, network nodes and qRT-PCR technical triplicates are not additional participants. External validation here means a small external expression-assay comparison, not validation of a clinical diagnostic or prognostic tool.

what_this_adds: A plasma vesicle-associated small-RNA expression resource for DCM with chronic heart failure.
A reported 92-feature differential set with computational target and pathway hypotheses.
External expression-assay assessment of 10 hub miRNAs, with a clear distinction from the discovery-stage miR-185-5p finding.

supports: DCM-HF-associated plasma exosomal miRNA expression differences in the studied samples.
An article-reported 92-feature screen and computational miRNA-target/pathway prioritization.
Small external qRT-PCR evaluation of a selected 10-miRNA panel.
Discovery-stage inclusion of hsa-miR-185-5p with the Table 1 values reported above.
does_not_establish: A prospectively validated early diagnostic test or prognostic model for DCM.
Causation of human DCM by the differential miRNAs or their predicted targets.
External qRT-PCR validation of miR-185-5p in this article.
Direct biochemical binding for every predicted miRNA-mRNA interaction.
Cardiac-cell origin or exclusive exosomal origin of every measured circulating RNA.
An effective miRNA-directed treatment in humans.

limitations: The discovery participant count is not reliably established from the reviewed text; no synthetic total is supplied.
The final Results screen uses absolute logFC >0.5, while Fig. 3A prints >0.05. P-value and FDR statements are not assumed to establish the same feature-wise threshold.

Methods 2.9 includes an abdominal-aortic-wall/mRNA extraction passage inconsistent with the surrounding plasma-exosomal-miRNA assay description; this is retained as a reporting limitation, not reinterpreted as a myocardial tissue experiment.
External evaluation is small (10 cases and 6 controls), and multivariate separation is not prospective diagnostic validation.
Some feature labels retain homolog/isomiR-style naming in the source; the complete feature set is not relabeled as uniquely verified canonical human mature miRNAs.

qa.question: What kind of DCM evidence does this paper provide?
qa.answer: Human case-control plasma miRNA expression profiling with an external assay phase; it is not a treatment trial or prospective prediction study.

qa.question: How many differential miRNA features were reported?
qa.answer: The final Results screen reports 92 features, split into 48 upregulated and 44 downregulated, using absolute logFC >0.5 and P<0.05. Fig. 3A prints a different logFC threshold; this discrepancy is not silently reconciled.

qa.question: Were the predicted pathways and miRNA targets experimentally established?
qa.answer: No. Target, enrichment and network analyses nominate relationships; the 55-node, 59-edge miRNA-mRNA network does not establish direct target binding or pathway causality.

qa.question: What was evaluated in the external population?
qa.answer: Ten selected hub miRNAs were assessed by qRT-PCR in 10 DCM patients and 6 healthy controls. Expression-distance and PCoA analyses supported group differences, not clinical diagnostic utility.

qa.question: Was miR-185-5p one of the externally tested hub miRNAs?
qa.answer: No. It appears in Table 1 with logFC 1.04 and P=0.0322 and in the predicted-network discussion, but is absent from the 10-miRNA external qRT-PCR list.

qa.question: Can the results be treated as a measured whole-plasma or myocardial tissue signature?
qa.answer: No. The reported study concerns isolated plasma vesicle-associated RNA. It does not establish myocardial origin or interchangeability with whole-plasma RNA measurements.

related_papers.relationship: Complementary DCM-HF plasma vesicle RNA profiling focused on circRNAs rather than miRNAs. Neither paper establishes that the two assays form a combined validated test or that their participants are non-overlapping.

The later liposomal miR-185-5p inhibition article cites this expression study. The connection is observational candidate prioritization followed by separate preclinical intervention experiments, not proof of human therapeutic efficacy.
Related DCM-HF biomarker research at the plasma-protein level; its plasma Olink measurements are not interchangeable with vesicle-associated miRNA profiling.

provenance.review_basis: Published main text, tables and figure legends at the cited primary sources. No independent reanalysis of participant-level data; unresolved reporting differences are identified in the evidence scope.
provenance.data_availability: Methods 2.8 states that raw sequencing data were uploaded to GEO, but no specific accession was verified from the reviewed text. The data-availability section also offers data on request. No accession or direct dataset link is inferred.

evidence_page_notice: Author-controlled evidence page for this publication. The evidence synthesis below is distinct from the published abstract and does not replace the version of record. Reported inconsistencies are qualified rather than silently corrected.
